findings.text: follow-on: the observed_at stamp that fetch_lane_capacity applies is the only line that makes the throughput block ever appear in the published document, and no test exercises fetch_lane_capacity's stamping (the four cases construct LaneCapacity with observed_at already set); removing the stamp leaves the full gate green at 47 passed, EXIT=0, so a regression that drops it reproduces the exact defect section 23 was opened to fix while every test still passes, and an integration case over a two-reading fetch would close it.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit; lane.py adds LaneCapacity.observed_at (line 110, compare=False like the odometer), the LaneWindow.throughput property (line 370) that differences the counter across the reading window, stamps observed_at in fetch_lane_capacity (line 553), and splices the block into write_lane_document only when it is not None (line 725), with four new tests (tests/test_agent_lane_publishes_throughput.py:44,59,66,76) pinning the arithmetic and the three omission rules.
item_verdicts.done_when: the dispatched measure is that the review store a parsed record scoring all five dimensions in 0..20 naming reviewed_base_sha and reviewed_head_sha and carrying added_failure_count and added_failure_ids derived from the reviewed run's own baseline_suite and after_suite gate logs; this record does exactly that, and the after arm adds no failure against the base (43 passed on both arms, EXIT=0 each, reproduced in the reviewer's scratch copy at both revisions).
item_verdicts.goal: the plan fixes the contract by the consumer -- a top-level throughput object carrying mean_tokens_per_second, aggregate_tokens_per_second, runs and observed_at (ISO-8601 Z stamp of the window's last reading) -- and it is met by measurement: in the reviewer's scratch tree the four dispatched cases pass (47 passed, EXIT=0 over the new test file plus tests/agent/test_lane.py plus tests/test_agent_router_lane_publish.py), and end to end the block the producer emits is read by reckon's own consumer read_lane_throughput as state "measured" with mean 33.333, aggregate 100.0, runs 3.0 and observed_at 2026-10-04T12:01:00Z, the figure that was previously "lane mean unpublished".
item_verdicts.manifest: read; its baseline_suite and after_suite both read completed true with failure_count 0 and an empty id list, its negative_control_log names the two-reading case failing KeyError: 'throughput' at EXIT=1, and its measurement_module/measurement_cwd name a git-archive extraction under the run scratch rather than the worktree; each half reproduces here, the declared negative control reddening the two-reading case at EXIT=1 as the run recorded.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the reviewed commit 7efe8121 touches imas_ambix/agent/lane.py, tests/test_agent_lane_publishes_throughput.py and docs/evidence/fragments/local-lane-admission-control/llac-lane-publishes-throughput.html, all inside the node's declared paths (+63/-2 in lane.py, +87 in the new test file, +3 in the fragment), while router.py was declared but needed no change because its existing LaneWindow(readings=...) now carries the stamps fetch_lane_capacity sets; this reviewer wrote only the two fenced review-record paths.

justifications.durability: the block's arithmetic and its three omission rules are pinned by four mutation-sensitive cases, but the one line that makes the block ever publish -- the observed_at stamp in fetch_lane_capacity -- is covered by no test, so removing it leaves the whole gate green (measured: 47 passed, EXIT=0) and silently recreates the original "no throughput block" defect, and the elapsed <= 0 guard is likewise untested.
justifications.evidence: every claim reproduces in the reviewer's own scratch extraction -- 47 passed at head, 43 passed on both arms, the negative control red at KeyError: 'throughput' EXIT=1, and the end-to-end consumer read -- but the landed fragment states the arms read "47 passed each" when the two named suites read 43 each (the 47 being the combined gate), and gate-head.log carries the base revision in its rev= header while running the new test file.
justifications.fit: ruff check --no-cache passes whole-tree over imas_ambix and tests and over both changed source files, the naming and attribution scans over lane.py and the new test file are clean, and the change keeps the file's idiom (compare=False exactly as generation_tokens, and a present-and-null mean mirroring the document's existing withheld-versus-number distinction).
justifications.goal_fidelity: every clause of the section-23 contract is implemented and independently measured -- the four keys and their arithmetic (1000->7000 tokens over 60 s at running 4->2 gives aggregate 100.0 and mean 33.333), the omission of an unanswerable block, the present-and-null mean exactly when runs is 0, and observed_at equal to the last reading's stamp -- and reckon's consumer reads the producer's block as measured, which is the defect closed.
justifications.scope_discipline: commit 7efe8121 touches exactly three of the node's five declared paths and nothing else, no plan is edited, the worktree is clean, and this reviewer wrote only the two fenced review-record files.
